reasoning: As of March 2026, SpaceX has conducted several Starship test flights (IFT-1 through IFT-6 by late 2024), but none were planned orbital missions - they were suborbital tests. The question specifically asks about the first flight planned to reach orbit. SpaceX has been incrementally testing, and an orbital attempt would require successful stage separation, Starship reaching orbital velocity, and completing at least one Earth orbit. Given SpaceX's iterative approach and the complexity involved, plus that no orbital flight plan has been officially announced yet, the probability of success on the very first orbital attempt is moderate but not high given historical rocket development challenges.
